History panel

From return planning onward this scenario departs from the historical record. The two selectable return opportunities, the control-reserve warning, the recovery conditions, the crew-condition variations, the controllers' reactions, and the next-mission constraints are fictional game modeling (F7, F8, F9). The post-flight stance and its relationship consequences are fictional (F10). The historical opening — docking, the communications gap, the crew's stabilization of the spacecraft, the termination rule, and a western Pacific recovery — follows the sources H1–H4.
Historical sources
H1 — Gemini's First Docking Turns to Wild Ride in Orbit (NASA, Bob Granath).

Supports the communication gap, crew stabilization and contingency return. It describes an orbit before historical recovery; it does not validate our two-option menu or invented extra-orbit margin. Its fault-cause wording is cautious. Used for the historical opening, not to claim simulated reserve telemetry or alternate crew conditions occurred.
H2 — 55 Years Ago: Gemini VIII, the First Docking in Space (NASA, John Uri).

Supports ending the remaining objectives after RCS activation and the western Pacific contingency recovery. It describes a next-available-opportunity rule. Our fictional choice does not establish that both game opportunities met the real rule. Its inconsistent ship initials and unneeded precise recovery details are not used.
H3 — Project Gemini: A Chronology, Part III(B), March 16 entry (NASA SP-4002).

Supports the approximate docking anchor and broad termination/recovery sequence. The source's cited original mission-report pages have not been independently checked. This is not transcript-verified content.
H4 — Gemini VIII mission overview (NASA).
Crew/context cross-check. Earlier review found inconsistent caption/time/bearing details; these are not used in the scenario's exact timeline.
H5 — 'Tumbling End Over End': The Trauma of Gemini VIII (Part 2), March 16, 2014 (Ben Evans, AmericaSpace).

User-supplied secondary account. Its post-flight discussion supports the attributed positions summarized in the context card, including the reported exoneration. The original memoir/interview passages and timing of each criticism have not been independently verified. No direct quotes are invented; the scene is not presented as a documented meeting. H5 does not support any numerical relationship adjustment or Glen's alternate response.
Fiction register

F1 — Contact rehearsal. Supplemental sender/acknowledgement exercise, readback document and its later ground handoff effects. These are performed fictional rehearsals, not astronaut training prerequisites.
F2 — Recovery rehearsal. Supplemental pickup ownership/readback exercise and the fictional rework it can avoid. Preparation does not move recovery forces closer.
F3 — Systems rehearsal. Supplemental warning-routing exercise, its readback and its operational handoff effects. Preparation does not add control reserve or identify the hardware fault.
F4 — Air-support and surface-retrieval reports. Original abstract status reports, now supporting a real operational choice. No claim to historical ship/aircraft positions.

F5 — Recovery coordination events. The fictional ground ownership clarification, acknowledgement retry and pickup approach consequences. These are explicitly events of the game room, not errors by historical astronauts or operators.
F6 — Procedure adoption. Two original standing-procedure choices and their reference pages. Neither reverses the operational outcome or the next-mission rehearsal constraint.
